existing_authored_summary_fields.version_or_commit: RFC 5545, September 2009, with R02/R03 for verified errata
existing_authored_summary_fields.governing_conditions: UID is TEXT and identifies the component; RECURRENCE-ID defaults to DATE-TIME, matches master value type/local form, and identifies the original slot. EXDATE wins over RRULE/RDATE inclusions; duplicates collapse; an unsynchronized DTSTART/rule is undefined. INTERVAL is positive and defaults to 1. COUNT includes DTSTART; COUNT and UNTIL are mutually exclusive; UNTIL for TZID DATE-TIME DTSTART is UTC DATE-TIME and is inclusive. Missing recurrence fields derive from DTSTART. A matching VTIMEZONE must cover recurrence instances. Folds use the first instant; gaps use the preceding offset. DTEND gives exact recurrence duration; DURATION gives nominal duration, with day/week components differing across transitions. §3.2.20 preserves unknown VALUE-type data; generic readers may ignore extension properties. New VEVENTs need UID/DTSTAMP and, without METHOD, DTSTART.
existing_authored_summary_fields.applicability: Governs the offline interchange design. Product subset, raw-byte preservation, upsert keys, tombstones and UI input rejection are product decisions. The earlier skip-gap text must be read with R03 and the later computed-time paragraph.

existing_authored_summary_fields.governing_meaning: The BWF guidance distinguishes recommendation levels. BEXT Description and OriginatorReference have 256/32 ASCII-character limits; identifiers may point outward, with a pathname-security caution. FADGI interprets origination date/time locally, without unambiguous UTC. The ltxt recommendation permits tran and recommends ASCII free text linked to cue ranges, with termination/padding conditions. Its optional Code Page entry has an ISO 8859/1 fallback when CSET is absent or zero. Thus the ASCII recommendation is not proof of an ASCII-only implementation for every ltxt tool. These are embedding conditions, not a recorder-wide compatibility result.
existing_authored_summary_fields.applicability: Supports the bounded BWF profile and timed-transcript lead. The final’s short-segment choice is a pilot recommendation, not a normative length cap.

existing_authored_summary_fields.governing_subject_operation_default_unit: File-layout/package specification. Opaque payload octets remain accessible. Each payload manifest enumerates every payload file once; valid means complete and all manifest checksums verify. Creation/validation tools MUST support SHA-256 and SHA-512; creation SHOULD default to SHA-512. Payload-Oxum is optional OctetCount.StreamCount (8-bit bytes, number of payload files), not digest validation. Tag manifests are optional; when present they include payload manifests. Paths are relative to bag root, use slash separators and encode LF/CR/percent specially. Interoperability guidance is non-normative. Retention controls, logical asset identity, curator completeness and authenticity are outside these guarantees.
existing_authored_summary_fields.applicability_assessment: Supports chosen copied-directory pilot, arbitrary inventory payload, per-file reference and conditional tag protection. Custodian retention is local policy. Supports rejecting archive-digest completeness/provenance/recovery proof.
